# Identical-body paired cost can be strictly below twice ordinary depth

For a full-dimensional convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\), write
\[
f_K(y)=\inf_{u\ne0}|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y\}|
\]
for its ordinary **absolute** depth, and define the identical-body paired cost
\[
p_{KK}(y)=\inf_{\substack{u\ne0\\\tau\in\mathbb R}}
\left(
|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y+\tau\}|
+|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y-\tau\}|
\right).
\tag{1}
\]
Taking \(\tau=0\) always gives \(p_{KK}(y)\le2f_K(y)\). The reverse inequality is false, already for a rational three-dimensional pyramid and an interior rational point.

Specifically, let
\[
K=\{(x_1,x_2,z):0\le z\le1,\ |x_1|\le z,\ |x_2|\le z\},
\qquad V=|K|=\frac43,
\]
\[
c=\frac{19}{25},\qquad y=(0,0,c).
\tag{2}
\]
Then the exact all-normal ordinary depth and a paired upper certificate are
\[
\boxed{\quad
f_K(y)=\frac{6859}{15625}V,\qquad
p_{KK}(y)\le\frac{13428}{15625}V
<2f_K(y).
\quad}
\tag{3}
\]
The certified gap between \(2f_K(y)\) and the displayed paired cost is
\[
\frac{58}{3125}V>0.
\tag{4}
\]
We do not claim that the displayed paired cap minimizes (1). An upper certificate, together with the exact ordinary depth, suffices to disprove the identity.

The two-source cap has a genuine ambient realization: place the two copies of \(K\) at bases \(-1,+1\), and use a cap with margin \(z-c+\tau p\). The actual convex hull also has the middle fiber \(K\); that middle source is not part of the paired quantity (1). No original mixed-body fiber is silently erased in a depth conclusion, and no OC counterexample is asserted.

## 1. Every ordinary normal reduces to one explicit scalar family

Under the normalized uniform law on \(K\), write
\[
(x_1,x_2,z)=(ZU,ZV_0,Z),
\]
where \(U,V_0\) are independent uniforms on \([-1,1]\), and \(Z\) is independent with density \(3z^2\) on \([0,1]\). The Jacobian of this parameterization is \(z^2\), and its total volume is \(4/3\). The zero-height singularity is null.

Consider any through-point cap
\[
\alpha x_1+\beta x_2+\gamma(z-c)\ge0.
\tag{5}
\]
If \(\gamma=0\), its mass is \(V/2\): the reflection
\((x_1,x_2,z)\mapsto(-x_1,-x_2,z)\) exchanges the two sides, and the nonzero normal gives a null boundary. If \(\gamma<0\), its mass is the complement of a cap with positive \(\gamma\), again with a null three-dimensional boundary. Thus it remains to bound both sides of (5) when \(\gamma>0\).

Put \(W=(\alpha U+\beta V_0)/\gamma\). Conditional on \(W=w\), the cap is \(Z(1+w)\ge c\), with probability
\[
\phi(w)=
\begin{cases}
0,&1+w\le c,\\
1-\dfrac{c^3}{(1+w)^3},&1+w>c.
\end{cases}
\tag{6}
\]
The law of \(W\) is symmetric. More precisely, set
\[
A=\max\{|\alpha|,|\beta|\}/\gamma,\qquad
B=\min\{|\alpha|,|\beta|\}/\gamma.
\]
If \(A=B=0\), then \(W=0\). If \(B=0<A\), \(W\) is uniform on \([-A,A]\). If \(A\ge B>0\), the convolution density is
\[
f_W(w)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac1{2A},& |w|\le A-B,\\[2mm]
\dfrac{A+B-|w|}{4AB},&A-B\le |w|\le A+B,\\
0,&|w|>A+B.
\end{cases}
\]
Equivalently, there is the exact probability-mixture identity
\[
\operatorname{Law}(W)=
\int_{A-B}^{A+B}\operatorname{Unif}[-v,v]\,
\frac{v}{2AB}\,dv.
\tag{7}
\]
Its mixing mass is one, and integrating the uniform density gives precisely the displayed trapezoid. The endpoint \(v=0\) when \(A=B\) has no mixing atom. Consequently a lower bound on the average of (6) for **every** centered uniform interval, including its point-mass limit, is a bound for every normal in (5).

## 2. All base-facing caps have mass at least \(c^3V\)

Let
\[
Q(v)=\frac1{2v}\int_{-v}^v\phi(w)\,dw,\qquad v>0,
\quad Q(0)=1-c^3.
\]
Direct integration gives the complete two-regime formula
\[
Q(v)=
\begin{cases}
1-\dfrac{c^3}{(1-v^2)^2},&0\le v\le1-c,\\[3mm]
\dfrac{1+v-\frac32c+\frac{c^3}{2(1+v)^2}}{2v},
&v\ge1-c.
\end{cases}
\tag{8}
\]
In the first regime every conditional threshold is proper, apart from the harmless supporting equality at the endpoint. In the second regime the integrand vanishes for \(w\le c-1\); that interval must be retained in the denominator \(2v\).

The first expression is decreasing in \(v\). At \(v=1-c=6/25\),
\[
Q(6/25)-c^3=\frac{1002251}{15015625}>0.
\tag{9}
\]
For the second expression, exact expansion gives
\[
15625\cdot4v(1+v)^2[Q(v)-c^3]
=3814v^3+3253v^2-4936v+2484.
\tag{10}
\]
The quadratic \(3253v^2-4936v+2484\) has positive leading coefficient and discriminant
\[
(-4936)^2-4\cdot3253\cdot2484=-7957712<0.
\]
It is therefore strictly positive for all real \(v\), while \(3814v^3\ge0\) for \(v\ge0\). The denominator in (10) is positive on its second-regime domain. Hence
\[
Q(v)>c^3\qquad(v\ge0).
\tag{11}
\]
Mixture (7) proves the desired lower bound for every positive-\(\gamma\) cap.

## 3. All opposite caps also have mass at least \(c^3V\)

Let \(\psi=1-\phi\). For every \(v\ge0\), if \(v\le1-c\), both conditional cuts are unsaturated and convexity of \(x\mapsto x^{-3}\) gives
\[
\psi(v)+\psi(-v)
=c^3[(1+v)^{-3}+(1-v)^{-3}]
\ge2c^3.
\tag{12}
\]
If \(v>1-c\), then \(\psi(-v)=1\), and
\[
\psi(v)+\psi(-v)\ge1>2c^3,
\tag{13}
\]
because \(2c^3=13718/15625<1\). This includes \(v\ge1\), where an expression with a negative denominator must not be used: definition (6) already gives the correct saturated value.

Symmetry of \(W\) implies \(\mathbb E\psi(W)\ge c^3\). Thus every negative-\(\gamma\) cap has at least \(c^3V\) as well. The \(\gamma=0\) caps have mass \(V/2>c^3V\).

Every containing halfspace can be translated to pass through \(y\) while decreasing its mass. We have therefore treated all ordinary caps. The cap \(\{z\le c\}\) has exactly \(c^3V\), proving the first equality in (3).

## 4. A strict paired certificate, including a proper-cut variant

Take \(u=e_z\) and \(\tau=1-c=6/25\) in (1). The two thresholds are
\[
c+\tau=1,\qquad c-\tau=2c-1=\frac{13}{25}.
\]
The first cap is a supporting square face, of zero three-dimensional volume. The second cap has volume
\[
\left[1-\left(\frac{13}{25}\right)^3\right]V
=\frac{13428}{15625}V.
\]
Together with the exact ordinary-depth equality, this proves (3)–(4).

The strict gap persists with both cuts proper. Replace the shift by
\(\tau=6/25-\varepsilon\), \(0<\varepsilon\le1/1000\). Both thresholds,
\(1-\varepsilon\) and \(13/25+\varepsilon\), then lie strictly between zero and one. Their total normalized cost is
\[
C(\varepsilon)=2-(1-\varepsilon)^3-(13/25+\varepsilon)^3.
\tag{14}
\]
Since \(C'(\varepsilon)\le3\) on this interval,
\[
2c^3-C(\varepsilon)
\ge\frac{58}{3125}-\frac3{1000}
=\frac{389}{25000}>0.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus the failure does not rely on declaring a supporting face empty or on an open-cap convention.

## 5. A precise simplex region where equality does hold

The counterexample does not invalidate the following exact lower-diagonal case. Let \(T_d=\{X_i\ge0,\sum_iX_i\le1\}\), \(d\ge1\), and let \(r,s>0\). For the pair \(rT_d,sT_d\), at the common point \(y=a\mathbf1\), assume
\[
0\le a\le\frac{\min(r,s)}{d+1}.
\]
Then the true paired cost is
\[
\boxed{\quad
p_{rT_d,sT_d}(a\mathbf1)=2|T_d|(da)^d.
\quad}
\tag{16}
\]
For \(a>0\), both copies contain the same inner simplex
\(((d+1)a)T_d\), whose centroid is \(a\mathbf1\). The proved equal-body paired-centroid theorem in **candidate 732b11a769399016** gives the lower bound
\[
2\Gamma_d\,|T_d|((d+1)a)^d=2|T_d|(da)^d.
\]
The identical caps \(\sum_iX_i\le da\), with shift zero, attain it in both larger simplices. At \(a=0\), both caps are null supporting faces. This proves (16), including unequal outer radii. For \(r=s\), the exact ordinary lower-diagonal formula gives
\[
p_{rT_d,rT_d}(a\mathbf1)=2f_{rT_d}(a\mathbf1)
\]
on that stated segment. No all-point or all-simplex identity is inferred.

For an actual chain, summing separately minimized pair costs still discards the common ambient tilt linking different pairs. The new counterexample closes the unrestricted substitution \(p_{KK}=2f_K\); the exact restricted identity (16) pays only the explicitly selected paired sources.

The standard-library verifier **../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_identical_body_pair_below_ordinary_depth.py** checks the scalar identities, both regime bounds, the exact gap and proper-cut variant, and the centered-uniform mixture normalization. The all-normal argument is Sections 1–3 and is independent of any numerical search.
